Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN)  -- England international footballer Steven Gerrard was found not guilty of affray by a court in his home city on Friday. England international Steven Gerrard was cleared by a court in Liverpool of affray. The jury at Liverpool Crown Court took a little over an hour to clear Gerrard of charges relating to a fracas in a nightclub bar in the north-western of England city on December 29 of last year. They accepted the Liverpool captain's version that he acted in self defense in punching businessman Marcus McGhee. The 29-year-old was the only one of the seven defendants in the case to be cleared after an incident which was described by judge Henry Globe as an "explosion of violence." Gerrard spoke of his relief outside the court. "Can I just say how pleased I am with today's verdict," he said. "I'm glad to put this case behind me and I am really looking forward to the season ahead and concentrating on my football now. "I would just like to say a big thank you to my legal team and to my friends and family and everyone at Liverpool football club for supporting me." His comments were met with a round of applause from a large group of fans of the Premier League club who had gathered outside the court, before he was ushered away. Gerrard was celebrating in the Lounge Inn in Southport, a suburb of Liverpool, after scoring twice his team's 5-1 win at Newcastle which took them to the top of the Premier League. Video footage, which was available to the court, showed the moment around 2.am in the morning when trouble flared. Gerrard apparently wanted to change the music on the CD player and the 34-year-old McGee said the football star had acted aggressively in trying to grab the device. In the fracas which followed, Gerrard admitted throwing three punches but said only one connected. He claimed, and his version was accepted by the jury, that he believed he was about to be attacked himself. "You did not start the violence, it was started by the violent elbowing of Marcus McGee in the face by one of your friends, John Doran," Globe said. "The victim's consequential actions of reeling backwards and then forwards and your actions in response to that movement forward has to be seen against that background," he added. Five other men have already pleaded guilty to affray and another admitted a lesser charge of threatening behavior. They will be sentenced at a later date.

**(CNN)** — England international footballer Steven Gerrard was found not guilty of affray by a court in his home city on Friday.

The jury at Liverpool Crown Court deliberated for a little over an hour before clearing Gerrard of charges stemming from an altercation at a nightclub bar in the north-western English city on December 29 of last year. The jurors accepted the Liverpool captain's account that he had acted in self-defense when he punched businessman Marcus McGhee.

The 29-year-old was the only one of the seven defendants in the case to be acquitted following an incident that Judge Henry Globe described as an "explosion of violence."

Speaking outside the court, Gerrard expressed his relief. "Can I just say how pleased I am with today's verdict," he said. "I'm glad to put this case behind me, and I am really looking forward to the season ahead and concentrating on my football now.

"I would just like to say a big thank you to my legal team, to my friends and family, and to everyone at Liverpool Football Club for supporting me."

His remarks were greeted with applause from a large group of the Premier League club's supporters who had gathered outside the court, before he was ushered away.

Gerrard had been celebrating at the Lounge Inn in Southport, a suburb of Liverpool, after scoring twice in his team's 5-1 victory at Newcastle—a result that propelled them to the top of the Premier League.

Video footage presented to the court captured the moment around 2 a.m. when the trouble erupted. Gerrard had reportedly wanted to change the music on the CD player, and the 34-year-old McGhee alleged that the footballer had behaved aggressively while attempting to seize the device.

In the ensuing scuffle, Gerrard admitted to throwing three punches but maintained that only one made contact. He claimed—and the jury accepted his version—that he believed he was about to be attacked himself.

"You did not start the violence; it was started by the violent elbowing of Marcus McGhee in the face by one of your friends, John Doran," Judge Globe said. "The victim's consequential actions of reeling backwards and then forwards, and your actions in response to that movement forward, have to be seen against that background," he added.

Five other men have already pleaded guilty to affray, and another admitted to the lesser charge of threatening behavior. They will be sentenced at a later date.

(CNN) -- On Friday, a court in his hometown acquitted England international footballer Steven Gerrard of the charge of affray. The Liverpool star was found innocent at a court in Liverpool.

It took the jury at Liverpool Crown Court just over sixty minutes to find Gerrard innocent of charges stemming from a brawl that occurred in a nightclub bar in this northwestern English city on December 29 of the previous year. The jurors believed the Liverpool captain's account that he had punched businessman Marcus McGhee in self-defense.

Out of the seven people charged in connection with what Judge Henry Globe called an "explosion of violence," the 29-year-old was the sole defendant to be found not guilty.

Standing outside the courthouse, Gerrard expressed his relief. "I just want to say how happy I am about the verdict today," he stated. "It's a relief to have this matter resolved, and now I'm eager to focus on my football and the upcoming season."

"I want to give my sincere thanks to my lawyers, as well as to my family, my friends, and everyone connected with Liverpool football club for standing by me," he continued.

A sizeable crowd of supporters of the Premier League team, who had assembled outside the court, cheered and applauded his remarks before he was quickly led away.

The court was shown video recordings that captured the moment the disturbance broke out at roughly 2 a.m. It appeared that Gerrard was trying to switch the music on the CD player, and the 34-year-old McGhee claimed the footballer had behaved aggressively while attempting to seize the machine.

During the ensuing scuffle, Gerrard acknowledged he threw three punches, though he insisted that only one landed. He argued—and the jury accepted his explanation—that he thought he was about to be assaulted himself.
